claims.text: Helm is a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
Helm is open source under Apache License 2.0 and the Helm project does not ship a commercial tier.
In Pulumi, resource ordering is derived from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready, and independent resources deploy in parallel.
Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind (per kind_sorter.go), and chart authors cannot declare dependencies between resources or subcharts except through hook weights.
Failed Pulumi updates leave the stack in a partially-updated state; `pulumi up` reconciles toward desired state and `pulumi refresh` detects drift.
Helm SDK is available in Go only; other languages must shell out to the helm CLI.

Pulumi Policies is open source, with rules in Python, TypeScript, or OPA Rego; Pulumi Cloud adds centralized policy management; the Enterprise edition adds Pulumi-maintained policy packs for CIS, PCI DSS, HITRUST, and NIST.
Helm has no native policy engine; policy is typically delegated to Kubernetes admission controllers such as Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper.
Pulumi is open source under Apache License 2.0.

The Helm docs state that "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's kind_sorter.go hardcoded install order begins with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with any kind not on the list (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the same kind-ordered list in reverse.
Helm sends sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and doesn't wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm chart dependencies merge a subchart's objects into the parent chart's set sorted by kind, so a chart can't express installing one subchart before another.
Helm hooks ordered with helm.sh/hook-weight annotations produce resources that Helm doesn't manage as part of the release.
Native sequencing for resources and subcharts has been proposed in HIP-0025, which is still a draft.
Passing one resource's output into another, or setting the dependsOn resource option, creates an edge in the Pulumi dependency graph.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to become ready before creating dependents and deploys independent resources in parallel; deletes follow the graph in reverse.
Pulumi's helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for dependencies on outside resources.
Helm records each install or upgrade as a numbered release revision, and helm rollback restores a prior revision.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Pulumi and Helm together.
Pulumi resolves chart values at deploy time and orders the chart install after its dependencies.
Pulumi creates and deletes resources in dependency order, with each resource ready before dependents, rather than fixed order by kind.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program is the most common adoption pattern.
Charts can be converted to native Pulumi code by rendering with helm template and converting the YAML with `pulumi convert --from kubernetes`.
`pulumi import` and the `import` resource option generate corresponding code.
A Pulumi program can pull charts from any Helm repository (public or private) and pass values as typed Pulumi inputs including outputs from other resources.
helm.v4.Chart renders templates locally and registers each Kubernetes object as an individual Pulumi resource, so every child shows up in plan output, drift detection, and state.
helm.v3.Release uses the embedded Helm SDK and creates a real Helm release in the cluster, preserving chart hooks, post-rendering, and release history.
Helm merges objects from a chart and its dependencies into a single set, sorts by Kubernetes kind, and applies in that order, so declaring a subchart as a dependency doesn't make it install first.
Pulumi's chart `values` input accepts the same shape as values.yaml but lets each leaf be a Pulumi output, and Pulumi installs the chart after the resources it depends on.
